chapters.title: Chapter 1: Two Different Businesses Under One Name

lessons.title: The Indian Market Today: Housing, Grade A Offices, Retail and Warehousing

children.text: In 2025, housing sales across India's seven biggest cities fell 14%. In the same year, office leasing hit an all-time record for the third year running, and warehouse leasing set a record too. If "real estate" were one market, those headlines could not all be true. They are true because residential, offices, retail and warehousing run on different engines. Before you pick a side, you need to know what powers each one today.

body.text: Indian real estate is not one cycle. Housing runs on household incomes and loan rates, offices on corporate hiring, retail on shoppers, and warehouses on supply chains. They can boom and slump in the same year.

children.text: Housing: Fewer Homes, Higher Prices

markDefs.definition: A shift in sales towards larger, more expensive homes, while the share of affordable housing shrinks. Total sales value can rise even as the number of units falls.

children.text: According to ANAROCK, the seven largest cities sold about 3.96 lakh homes in 2025, down 14% from roughly 4.6 lakh in 2024. Yet the value of those sales rose 6% to about ₹6 lakh crore, and average prices rose around 8%. Fewer homes were sold, but each one cost more. That pattern is called
premiumisation
: developers launch more luxury and upper-mid projects, while affordable housing loses share.

Chennai was the only one of the seven to grow. Hyderabad fell 23% and Pune 20%. ANAROCK linked the slowdown to IT layoffs, tariff tensions and geopolitical uncertainty, which is a reminder that housing demand depends on how secure buyers feel about their jobs.

body.text: For a residential investor, prices rising faster than rents is a warning sign, not a victory. If a flat's price rises 8% while its rent rises 5%, its rental yield shrinks. Your return then depends even more on the next buyer paying more.

children.text: Grade A Offices: A Record Built on Global Companies

markDefs.definition: The total office space leased in a period, including tenants relocating between buildings. It is usually higher than net absorption, which counts only the net increase in occupied space.
The change in occupied space over a period: space newly occupied minus space vacated. It shows real growth in demand.

children.text: Office demand has moved in the opposite direction. JLL put 2025
gross leasing
at 83.3 million sq ft and CBRE at 82.6 million sq ft, both records. JLL estimated
net absorption
at 57 million sq ft. Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi NCR led the take-up.

markDefs.definition: In-house centres set up in India by multinational companies to run technology, analytics, finance, engineering and other functions for their global business.

children.text: The biggest single driver is
Global Capability Centres (GCCs)

. Their share of office leasing, which had dipped below 30% in 2022, climbed back to nearly 40% in 2025. When a global bank or chipmaker builds a 5,000-seat campus in Hyderabad, it signs a long lease in a Grade A tech park.

body.text: A record office leasing headline does not mean every office unit in the city is in demand. GCCs and large corporates want big floor plates in professionally managed Grade A parks, not a small unit in an ageing building.

markDefs.definition: Ownership of an individual unit or floor within a larger building, with the rest of the building owned by many different parties. Common for small office units and shops bought by individuals.

children.text: That distinction matters. Most of this Grade A stock sits in large campuses owned by developers, listed REITs and institutional investors. What an individual can usually buy is a
strata-titled
office unit in a building with many owners. Those buildings are often older, less professionally managed and less attractive to GCCs, so the headline demand does not automatically reach them.
Retail: High Streets and Malls

Retail leasing rebounded strongly in 2025. Estimates from different consultants range from about 8.9 to 12.5 million sq ft, the highest in three years. High streets took roughly 48% of leasing and malls about 45%. Apparel led demand, followed by entertainment, supermarkets and food and beverage brands.

The segment is sharply split by quality. Well-located Grade A malls, such as those held by Nexus Select Trust, stay full and push rents up. Poorly located or badly managed malls in the same city can sit half-empty for years. For individual investors, the most common entry point is a high-street shop, which is easy to understand but depends heavily on footfall on one particular street.
Warehousing: Riding E-commerce and Manufacturing

markDefs.definition: Companies that run warehousing, transport and distribution for other businesses, such as e-commerce platforms and consumer goods makers.

children.text: Industrial and warehousing leasing reached about 37 million sq ft across the top eight cities in 2025, a record and roughly 16% higher than 2024. Delhi NCR led with 7.3 million sq ft, followed by Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Kolkata.
Third-party logistics (3PL)
firms took about 32% of Grade A space, and engineering and e-commerce together made up about 35%.

Two policy shifts built this market. GST, from July 2017, removed the need for a warehouse in every state to avoid inter-state taxes, so companies consolidated into large, modern hubs. Manufacturing incentives then added factories that need storage close by. Grade A warehousing is overwhelmingly owned by institutional park developers, so individuals mostly get exposure indirectly.

children.text: How the Commercial Market Became Investable
Ten years ago, an Indian retail investor had almost no clean way to own Grade A commercial property. Regulation changed that step by step.

body.title: Milestones that opened commercial real estate to investors

events.title: SEBI notifies REIT regulations
events.description: Creates the legal framework for listed trusts that own rent-producing property.

events.title: RERA enacted and made operational
events.description: Brings registration, escrow and disclosure rules to developers, mainly transforming residential projects.

events.title: GST launched
events.description: Consolidates fragmented state-wise warehousing into large modern hubs.

events.title: Embassy Office Parks REIT lists
events.description: India's first REIT, giving public investors a share in Grade A office parks.

events.description: Office REIT options widen across Mumbai, Hyderabad, Pune, NCR and Kolkata.

body.title: Quick Check: Reading the Housing Numbers
body.question: In 2025, housing sales in India's top seven cities fell 14% by units but rose 6% by value. What best explains this?
options: Developers cut prices to clear unsold stock
Fewer homes were sold, but the mix shifted towards more expensive homes and average prices rose
More affordable homes were sold than in 2024
The data counts commercial property in sales value
body.explanation: Units fell while value rose because average prices rose about 8% and sales tilted towards premium homes. Price cuts or a shift to affordable homes would push value down, not up.

body.title: Calculate: Mumbai's Share of Housing Sales
body.prompt: MMR sold 1,27,875 homes in 2025, out of 3,95,625 across the top seven cities. What percentage of total sales did MMR account for? Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: 1,27,875 ÷ 3,95,625 × 100 = 32.3%. Nearly one in three homes sold in India's biggest seven cities was in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Office Demand Engine
body.textWithBlank: In-house centres run by multinationals, which drove nearly 40% of India's office leasing in 2025, are called Global ___ Centres.
body.explanation: Global Capability Centres (GCCs) handle technology, analytics, finance and engineering work for their parent companies, and they lease large Grade A campuses on long leases.

body.title: Scenario: Buying the Headline
body.scenario: An investor in Bengaluru reads that office leasing hit a record 83 million sq ft in 2025, led by GCCs. A broker offers him a 900 sq ft strata office unit on the third floor of a 20-year-old building on a busy Koramangala road, with 11 different owners. It is currently vacant. He decides the record demand means it will lease quickly.
body.prompt: Is his reasoning sound? What should he check first?
body.modelAnswer: Not yet. The record leasing is concentrated in large Grade A campuses that GCCs and big corporates prefer: large floor plates, modern amenities, single professional management and good power backup. A 20-year-old strata building with 11 owners competes in a very different pool of small tenants such as local firms, clinics and startups. He should check actual vacancy in that building and on that stretch, how long comparable units took to lease, the rent they achieved, who manages common areas and maintenance, and whether the building has the fire and occupancy approvals larger tenants insist on. If he wants exposure to the demand the headline describes, a REIT that owns Grade A campuses is a more direct route.

cards.definition: A shift in housing sales towards larger, pricier homes, so total sales value rises even as units sold fall.
Total office space leased in a period, including tenants relocating between buildings.
Space newly occupied minus space vacated over a period; the truer measure of demand growth.
A multinational's in-house centre in India handling technology, analytics, finance or engineering work.
An individually owned unit inside a building with many owners, the typical commercial buy for individuals.
Firms that run warehousing and distribution for other businesses; the largest users of Grade A warehouses.

points: Residential, office, retail and warehousing follow different demand drivers and can move in opposite directions in the same year.
Housing sales in the top seven cities fell 14% to about 3.96 lakh units in 2025, while value rose 6% as prices and premium demand climbed.
Office gross leasing hit a record of about 83 million sq ft in 2025, with GCCs driving nearly 40% of demand.
Retail is split by quality: strong malls and high streets thrive while weak malls struggle.
Warehousing leasing reached a record of about 37 million sq ft, powered by 3PL, e-commerce and manufacturing.
Most Grade A commercial stock is institutionally owned, so headline demand does not automatically reach small strata units.

body.text: Market figures are for calendar year 2025 unless stated, drawn from published reports by ANAROCK, JLL, CBRE and other property consultants. Consultants define markets differently, so their numbers vary. This lesson is educational and is not a recommendation to buy any property or security.
